public_rationale: The evidence supports the financial strain behind the statement, but does not settle the whole claim on a consistent measure. CNBC confirmed an expected $5 billion OpenAI loss for 2024. Anthropic's later filing reports $5.692 billion of operating cash outflow for that year. Those are different measures, and the OpenAI figure was a forecast. Reported OpenAI cash burn of $340 million in the first half also shows why losses cannot simply be relabeled cash burn; it does not settle the annual total. The further claim about having found no way to stop lacks a clear test. A firm verdict would depend on supplying a financial definition and a standard for that clause.
limitations: This assessment concerns the position described in February 2025, not the companies' subsequent performance.
OpenAI evidence here relies on reporting rather than accessible underlying financial statements.
The Anthropic filing supplies retrospective evidence but was unavailable when the post appeared.
The combined claim is unresolved; this does not establish that either company was profitable.

our_interpretation: The ordinary contextual reading is that each company incurs annual financial losses of multiple billions of dollars. Zitron explicitly includes noncash costs, so a cash-flow-only reading would omit part of his meaning.
Use calendar 2024, the latest completed annual period before the post. The surrounding discussion refers to that year's financial figures.
Interpret 'billions' as at least $2 billion for each company separately, not their combined total.
Interpret the second clause as an observation about a demonstrated route to ending losses as of publication, not a prediction that either company can never become profitable.
Cash burn, operating losses, net losses and gross compute spending must remain separate. Supporting the combined claim requires a defensible reconciliation of the measures used for both companies.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable 2024 financial evidence establishes at least $2 billion in annual losses for each company under the contextual interpretation, and contemporaneous evidence establishes that neither had demonstrated a sustainable route to ending those losses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable 2024 financial evidence establishes that either company's annual losses were below $2 billion, or contemporaneous evidence establishes a demonstrated sustainable route to ending losses that contradicts the second clause.
